isNotAReview: This document reviews no artifact, declares no subject, and carries no verdict, decision, blockingFindingCount or sealRecommendation. It must not be read as a review of any surface, of any checker, or of the predecessor sweep it composes with.
authority: None. This file is an instrument reading, not a contract. Nothing here may be cited to close a parked recipe, to justify authoring one, or to change any surface disposition. CD-RT-5 remains BLOCKED_ON_PHASE_1A; no [UNSET] was touched. Freeze section 7.6 relies on measurement-only documents being mechanically distinguishable from pins; the six fields above are that distinction.
purpose: Close the single largest declared blind spot of artifacts/uncomputable-identity-fields.sweep.v1.json, which recorded verbatim: 'RULES IN EXECUTABLE CODE. This sweep read *.py only to confirm two specific absences from JSON. It did NOT systematically sweep the 94 checkers for derivations that exist only in code. rawBytesCommitment, fixtureCommitment and indexFingerprint were each found this way, so the class is known to be non-empty and its true size in the checker corpus is UNMEASURED. That is the single largest known blind spot in this document.' This document measures that class.
theQuestionMeasured: For every identity/digest-typed field in the corpus, does a producing rule exist only inside checker Python? A rule living only in a .py file is invisible to every contract reader, and freeze section 7.2 pins those checkers' bytes, so the rule is simultaneously load-bearing and uncitable. An implementer reading only the contracts, as the litmus requires, cannot find it.

three_ruleGranularityRatherThanPositionG.statement: The predecessor counted declared field POSITIONS. Measured at the classification pass: 386 documents, 0 parse failures, 0 duplicate-key rejections. The corpus held 386 .json files including the predecessor sweep; this file is the 387th. howTheProducingRuleShapesWereDerived.principle: Not assumed from the brief's list. The brief named preimage constructions, domain separators, hashlib call sites, framing helpers and encode_*/commit*/derive_* functions. That set was used only to widen the net; the operative shapes were derived from the code by four independent mechanical axes whose UNION was taken, so a rule missed by one axis is still caught.
howTheProducingRuleShapesWereDerived.axis1_directHashCallSites: ast.walk over all 94 *.py collecting every Call whose func is an Attribute on the Name 'hashlib', with its enclosing function resolved through a class/function stack. Measured: 225 call sites in 83 files. 11 of the 94 files contain no hashlib call at all.
howTheProducingRuleShapesWereDerived.axis2_transitiveReachability: A per-file call graph was built and closed transitively, because the sharpest rules delegate: _raw_bytes_commitment contains no hashlib call and reaches one only through domain_digest. Measured: 189 functions contain a direct hashlib call; 1142 functions reach one transitively. This axis was necessary and is the reason the first two passes of this sweep UNDERCOUNTED -- recorded because the same omission would silently shrink any repetition of this measurement.
howTheProducingRuleShapesWereDerived.axis3_domainSeparatorLiterals: Every str/bytes Constant in every *.py was collected by ast (33335 distinct), then normalised by stripping trailing framing bytes (NUL, '/', '|', ':') because separators are written as 'opensip.rt15.fixture-run.v1\u0000' and 'opensip.rt15.fixture-semantic-binding.v1/' rather than bare. 184 are domain-separator shaped. THIS NORMALISATION WAS LOAD-BEARING: without it, five of the eight rt15 domains were invisible, including three this sweep newly reports.
howTheProducingRuleShapesWereDerived.axis4_nulBearingLiterals: Any literal CONTAINING a NUL byte is a domain-separated preimage prefix by construction. This axis is representation-level and completely name-independent, so no identifier spelling can hide from it. Measured: 23 such literals. It independently caught opensip.proof-obligation.v1, which axis 3 also caught, and confirmed that the rt15 bytes-closure and resolution-fixture domains are NOT NUL-bearing literals (the NUL is added inside domain_digest), which is why both axes were needed.
howTheProducingRuleShapesWereDerived.axis5_framingPrimitives: Regex census over the same functions for u64be/u32be/u16be/u8 length framing (to_bytes(n,'big'), struct.pack('>...')), NUL separators, json.dumps(sort_keys=...), separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii, deterministic CBOR, and Merkle folds. This axis catches producing rules that carry NO domain separator, which axes 3 and 4 cannot see. It is how availabilityCanonicalSha256 and the C-2 skeleton digest were found.
howTheProducingRuleShapesWereDerived.whyThatSetAndNotTheBriefs: The brief's set is name-driven and would have been defeated three times over in this corpus: by _semantic_ref (a producing rule whose name suggests a lookup), by _host_ref (three pinned identities behind a name that suggests a handle), and by document_skeleton_digest (a rule the predecessor had already excluded by category). Axes 3, 4 and 5 are representation-level and name-independent for exactly this reason.

howAbsenceWasEstablished.standard: No negative claim in this document rests on assumption. For every rule classified CODE-ONLY, absence was established by a search that is described here and reproducible: (a) the exact domain-separator string, and each of its normalised prefixes, was substring-searched across all 386 parsed .json documents and all 31 markdown surfaces (root *.md, architecture/, steering/, cleansheet/, deltas/); (b) the identity's field name was searched both as an object KEY and inside every string VALUE corpus-wide; (c) the value-side intersection was taken against the predecessor's rule vocabulary (preimage, domainSeparator, domainUtf8, domainTag, domainBytes, canonicaliz, SHA-256(, is computed, derived as, recipe, byte recipe, encoding, framing, 0x00). A rule is CODE-ONLY only when (a) returns zero non-measurement documents AND (c) is empty or contains solely input-set statements rather than byte constructions.
howAbsenceWasEstablished.theMeasurementArtifactExclusion: The predecessor sweep QUOTES two of these domain separators in its own evidence text. A naive substring test over artifacts/*.json therefore reports them as 'present in a JSON artifact'. They are not present in any CONTRACT: they are present in one measurement-only document that binds nothing. All cross-references in this sweep exclude artifacts/uncomputable-identity-fields.sweep.v1.json and this file. This is recorded because the naive test was run first and gave the wrong answer, and because it is exactly the shape of error that produced the 'nowhere stated' claim the freeze had to correct.
howAbsenceWasEstablished.quoteBeforeConcludingAbsence: Where a contract DOES say something adjacent, it is quoted in the row rather than suppressed, even when the quotation weakens the finding. evidence.v3 states the INPUT SET for proofObligationId and delivery.v2 states the CONSTRUCTION for cbor_commitment; both are quoted verbatim below, and they move those rows to different states.

method.rulesWereExecutedNotOnlyRead: Every CODE-ONLY row that produces a value the corpus pins was IMPLEMENTED FROM THE CHECKER SOURCE and executed against the contract's own pinned goldens. A rule that could not be executed is reported as read-but-unverified, not as confirmed. 41 independent value reproductions were performed and all 41 matched byte-exactly on the first attempt; they are listed in reproductionsPerformed. This is what distinguishes 'a function that looks like a producer' from 'the function that actually produced the pinned bytes'.
method.namesAreNotNatures: Classification is by what the code and the contracts DO. Applied in both directions and it changed the answer in both. REJECTED as producing rules despite identity-shaped domain literals: opensip.snapshot-id.v2 (check-resolved-inputs.py:2086), opensip.plan-intent.v2 (check-c2-v4.py:2628) and opensip.bodyhash.alternate (check-fact-identity.py:679) are all NEGATIVE-CONTROL MUTATIONS -- functions named _m_change_snapshot_domain, _m_change_intent_domain and _m_closure_changes_domain that corrupt a domain tag to prove the checker rejects it. Each is a domain separator appearing in zero JSON, and each would have been a false positive for a name- or domain-driven sweep. Also rejected: EP11/EP12/EP13-SENTINEL (poisoning values for mutation testing) and _code_fingerprint (a behavioural fingerprint of a served module, not a corpus identity). ADMITTED despite non-identity names: _semantic_ref and _host_ref, which produce five pinned digest-typed positions between them.

states.STATED-IN-CONTRACT: The checker implements a byte construction that a contract already states. The code is a reader of the contract, not its source. An implementer who never opens the .py can compute the value.
states.CODE-ONLY: The rule exists nowhere but in Python. No contract, review, adjudication or markdown surface states the domain separator, the framing, or the canonicalisation that produces the value. THIS IS THE CLASS.
states.CODE-ONLY-BUT-DERIVABLE: A contract states enough that the code is a faithful realisation rather than the sole source, but the assembly is not stated under the name the head uses, or one ingredient is reachable only through a golden vector rather than through a grammar. Distinguished carefully because it is the state most likely to be misjudged in either direction: over-calling it hides a real gap, under-calling it manufactures one.

codeOnly.severityNote: The WEAKEST row in this class and recorded as such. rows.predecessorRank: 'Second-highest unparked finding; it is pinned as a baseline on a binding head.'
rows.basis: The producing construction IS stated -- evaluation-proof.v7/v9 #/rawAuthorityRecordGrammar gives encoding, canonicalJson and digest; evaluation-proof.v7 #/evaluationAuthorityStoreIndex gives the closed field set; evaluation-proof.v6/v7/v8 authorityGoldens give the domainUtf8. rows.whatSurvives: The naming binding (that v13's indexFingerprint IS that ref) exists only in three checkers; EvaluationAuthorityIndexV1 is absent from the grammar's three-entry records list so the domain is reachable only via a golden; and the projectId is not pinned on v13's baseline. On the HEAD alone it is still not computable.
rows.whatChangesAboutClosingIt: It is a head-shedding defect, not a missing-recipe defect. The lawful repair is a derivedFrom or carriedFragments pointer from v13 to the grammar-bearing predecessor -- which is what C-2 v9 already does correctly -- rather than authoring a new recipe. Authoring one would DUPLICATE an existing rule and risk forking it.
rows.explicitNonClaim: This sweep does not assert the predecessor erred. It classified from the contract side under a stated method and recorded the .py evidence it had; the .py sweep it declined to do is the one that moves the row. That is the blind spot working as documented.

rows.basis: The predecessor identified the rule's location by inspection. This sweep transcribed it, executed it against retention-tiers.v22's own two pinned goldens, and matched both byte-exactly on the first attempt, establishing that _raw_bytes_commitment is not merely present in the checker but is the actual producer of the pinned bytes.
rows.addition: The sort key is request.recordCasRef and NOT the encoded RawObjectKeyV1 used elsewhere in the same grammar -- so even an implementer who correctly guessed 'sorted' would fork.

checkerImmutabilityOfTheseRules.whyThisSectionExists: A code-only rule inside a self-pinned checker cannot be lifted into a contract without a successor, which changes what closing it costs. Measured here rather than assumed.
checkerImmutabilityOfTheseRules.methodAndItsCorrection: Self-pinning was first detected by a regex that flagged any checker naming itself, and it returned six files. FOUR WERE FALSE POSITIVES -- check-evaluation-proof-v10/v11/v12/v13.py name themselves only in a docstring and a usage line. The corrected test requires the file's own basename to appear as the ARGUMENT of a hashing call in its own source. Recorded because the uncorrected figure disagreed with freeze section 7.6 and the disagreement was the instrument, not the corpus.
checkerImmutabilityOfTheseRules.agreementWithFreeze76: Exactly reproduces the freeze's statement 'Two of them self-pin', and the self-pin site is confirmed at check-phase1a-a-prime-successor-v3.py:166, verbatim: "sha256": sha_file("check-phase1a-a-prime-successor-v3.py").

This is the one piece of good news in this document: no rule measured here is in the strongest-immutability class, so none is unliftable for that reason.

runtimeHashVerification.measured: 71 of the 93 checkers contain an explicit runtime drift comparison (a computed digest compared against an expected constant, reported as 'protected input changed', 'dependency hash drift' or an expected/actual inequality).
runtimeHashVerification.allEightRetentionCheckersVerifyAtRuntime: check-retention-custody-v15..v22.py all hash-verify their dependencies at execution. This is the mechanism freeze section 7.6 describes when it records that seven of them exit 2 with AuthorityError before examining any contract if ARCHITECTURE-TO-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md moves by one byte.
runtimeHashVerification.consequenceForCO01throughCO08: The eight rt15 rules live in eight runtime-verifying checkers. They cannot be edited in place, but they are not self-pinned, so a successor contract could STATE them without touching the checkers at all -- the checkers would continue to pass, because stating a rule in a contract does not change the checker's inputs.

pinDensityOfTheRuleBearingCheckers.note: Count of OTHER files in docs/coop recording the checker's CURRENT bytes, excluding the seven self-declared measurement-only or record-only documents, per freeze section 7.6's own exclusion.
pinDensityOfTheRuleBearingCheckers.interpretation: Every checker carrying a code-only rule is pinned by at least four other documents. None can be edited. Lifting any of these rules is therefore necessarily an authoring act on a CONTRACT, never a repair of the checker -- which is consistent with this sweep proposing no recipe.

whatThisSweepCannotSee.preamble: A false negative here reads as coverage, which is this corpus's dominant failure mode -- freeze section 7 records 10+ instances. These are the boundaries of what this measurement establishes, stated so that the next lane inherits a named gap rather than an unearned sense of completeness.
limits: RULES BUILT FROM COMPUTED STRINGS. Every axis here reads LITERALS. A domain separator assembled at runtime from a variable, an f-string, a config lookup or a table join would be invisible to all five axes. This is not hypothetical in this corpus: CO-06's separator is a CONCATENATION ('opensip.rt15.fixture-semantic-binding.v1/' + semanticDomain) and was caught only because its constant prefix is a literal. A rule whose separator has NO literal prefix would be missed entirely, and this sweep cannot bound how many such rules exist.

SEMANTIC EQUIVALENCE OF FRAMING. Reproducing a pinned value proves the transcribed rule produces those bytes. It does not prove the transcription is the only rule that would, nor that the checker's rule is the RIGHT one, nor that it agrees with an unwritten intent. Where a golden cannot discriminate two readings, this sweep inherits the predecessor's nonDiscriminatingVectors finding unchanged and adds nothing.

THE STATED-IN-CONTRACT COLUMN IS A SAMPLE, NOT A CENSUS. Twelve rule families were verified against quoted contract text. The corpus contains more stated rules that were confirmed present and not itemised. A reader must NOT compute 'total rules minus stated equals code-only' from this document; the CODE-ONLY count is exhaustive over the searched shapes, the STATED count is not.

ABSENCE WAS TESTED BY SUBSTRING, NOT BY MEANING. A contract that states a rule in prose WITHOUT using the domain separator string or the field name -- for example by describing the construction narratively under a different heading -- would be scored absent. The predecessor recorded the mirror-image of this gap (unitSetCommitment is computable via a sibling key and has zero prose occurrences of its own name) and it is equally live here. Every CODE-ONLY row in this document is a claim that no such prose was found, not a proof that none exists.

CHECKER EXECUTION PATHS WERE NOT TRACED. Rules were read and re-implemented, not observed by instrumenting a run. A function that is defined but never reached, or reached only on a branch no vector exercises, is classified here as a rule on equal footing with one that produces a pinned value. CO-08 and CO-14 are the two rows where this most likely overstates: neither was reproduced against a pinned value, and the alternativeStricterCount exists so a reader can discount them.

NO CHECKER WAS EXECUTED AND NO EXIT CODE IS CITED AS EVIDENCE. This sweep ran only its own transcriptions, in scratch, against parsed contract data. It asserts no result about any checker's behaviour, and in particular it does not claim that any guard fired or did not fire.

SUPERSEDED LINEAGES WERE SWEPT FOR RULES, NOT CLASSIFIED EXHAUSTIVELY. All 94 .py files were read for producing rules, but where a rule recurs across a version lineage only the latest body was transcribed and executed, after confirming body-identity by normalised hash. A version whose body DIFFERS in a way the normalisation hid would be misattributed. Measured: for CO-01 through CO-07 all eight retention bodies hash identically after comment and whitespace normalisation; for CO-10..CO-12 the v7 and v8 bodies are identical.

MARKDOWN WAS SEARCHED, NOT READ. 31 markdown surfaces were substring-searched for every domain separator and identity name. They were not read for narrative statements of a rule that name neither. A rule stated only in freeze or blueprint prose, in terms matching neither the separator nor the field name, would be missed.

A LIVE CORPUS. 386 .json documents at every pass of this sweep, stable throughout, and 94 .py. Any artifact changed after this file was written is outside what it establishes. All digests quoted here were measured at read time.

NO INDEPENDENT REPLICATION. The 41 reproductions were performed once, by this sweep, with encoders transcribed from checker source by one reader. The two-encoder standard set by evidence-identity-recipes is NOT met by this document. A transcription error that happened to reproduce a pinned value is vanishingly unlikely 41 times, but the reproductions are not independent of each other: CO-02, CO-03, CO-04 and CO-06 all share the CO-01 primitive, so a misreading of domain_digest would have failed all of them together rather than being caught by one.

THE THREE-STATE BOUNDARY IS A JUDGEMENT AT ONE PLACE. CD-01 (indexFingerprint) and CO-09 (proofObligationId) sit on opposite sides of the same line: both have a contract that says SOMETHING. CD-01's contract states a byte construction and a closed field set, so the code realises it; CO-09's states an input list only, so the code is the sole source of the bytes. A reader who disagrees with that boundary should move CO-09 to DERIVABLE and read CODE-ONLY as 13. The evidence for both is quoted in full in the rows so the judgement can be checked rather than inherited.
